```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(AlphaSimR); library(data.table); library(Matrix); library(nadiv)
  library(sommer); library(rrBLUP); library(BGLR); library(ggplot2); library(knitr)
})
set.seed(params$seed)
t0 <- Sys.time()

# progress log (knitr discards message() output when message = FALSE)
progress <- function(...) cat(format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), ..., "\n",
                              file = file.path(params$sim_dir, "progress.log"), append = TRUE)
```

# Overview

Input: the populations simulated in `01_founders_burnin.Rmd` (folder ``r params$sim_dir``).
Everything here is computed from that simulation; nothing is typed in by hand.

| Model | Relationship / prior | Predicts EBV from | Variance components |
|---|---|---|---|
| ABLUP | pedigree A^-1^ (nadiv, with inbreeding) | pedigree | REML (sommer) |
| GBLUP | VanRaden G | genomic relationships, then back-solved **SNP effects** | REML (sommer) |
| ssGBLUP | H^-1^ = A^-1^ + [0, 0; 0, G~b~^-1^ - A~22~^-1^] | pedigree + genotypes | REML (sommer) |
| ssGBLUP_MF | H^-1^ with breed metafounders: (A^Γ^)^-1^ + [0, 0; 0, G~05b~^-1^ - (A^Γ^~22~)^-1^] | pedigree + genotypes | REML (sommer) |
| wssGBLUP | H^-1^ with SNP-weighted G (Wang et al. 2012) | as ssGBLUP | REML (sommer) |
| rrBLUP | ridge on SNP | **SNP effects** | REML (rrBLUP::mixed.solve) |
| BayesA | scaled-t SNP effects | **SNP effects** | MCMC (BGLR) |
| BayesB | point-mass + scaled-t | **SNP effects** | MCMC (BGLR) |

Fixed effects in every model: **breed** (factor) + **herd x generation** (block; herd effects
were redrawn every generation in file 01, and herds are nested in country). Since 7 Nov 2026 the
herds are single-breed (CFIT farms, file 00), so herd x generation also identifies the breed; the
breed term is then dropped as redundant (same fit, full-rank design).

# Load simulation output

```{r load}
st   <- readRDS(file.path(params$sim_dir, "burnin_state.rds"))
SP   <- st$SP                               # needed by AlphaSimR accessors
phen <- fread(file.path(params$sim_dir, "phenotypes.csv"))
ped  <- fread(file.path(params$sim_dir, "pedigree.csv"))
traits <- st$traits
h2_par <- fread("params/h2.csv")
gens <- sort(unique(as.integer(sub(" .*", "", names(st$kept_cows)))))
cat("Generations with saved genomes:", gens, "\n")
```

# Sampling design (subsample for the G-based models)

Stratified by **breed x country** within each generation, proportional to the number of cows.

```{r sample}
strat_sample <- function(dt, n) {
  dt[, k := pmax(1, round(n * .N / nrow(dt))), by = .(breed, country)]
  out <- dt[, .SD[sample(.N, min(.N, k[1]))], by = .(breed, country)]
  out[, k := NULL]; out
}
cand <- phen[generation %in% gens]
geno_ids <- rbindlist(lapply(gens, function(g)
  strat_sample(copy(cand[generation == g]), params$n_geno_per_gen)))$id
ng_pool  <- cand[generation %in% head(gens, -1) & !(id %in% geno_ids)]
nongeno_ids <- strat_sample(copy(ng_pool), params$n_nongeno)$id

dat <- phen[id %in% c(geno_ids, nongeno_ids)]
dat[, genotyped := id %in% geno_ids]
dat[, hg := factor(paste(herd, generation, sep = "_g"))]
dat[, breed := factor(breed)]
dat[, .N, by = .(generation, genotyped)][order(generation, -genotyped)]
dcast(dat[genotyped == TRUE], breed ~ country, fun.aggregate = length, value.var = "id")
```

# Dosage matrix and its transformations

AlphaSimR returns SNP genotypes as **allele dosages** (count of allele "1": 0, 1, 2).
Three codings are used below, and they are algebraically equivalent for prediction:

* `M`: dosage 0/1/2.
* `W = M - 1`: -1/0/1 coding (as in `rrBLUP::A.mat`).
* `Z = M - 2p`: centred by allele frequency (VanRaden 2008, method 1).

```{r dosage}
# 8 Nov 2026 (memory, 7 GB machine): subset every saved generation to the sampled cows BEFORE merging,
# and drop the last-generation population that this file does not use. Same cows, same order as before.
st$pop <- NULL
gid <- as.character(geno_ids)
all_cows <- do.call(c, unname(lapply(st$kept_cows, function(p) p[p@id %in% gid])))
st$kept_cows <- NULL; invisible(gc())
gpop <- all_cows[match(gid, all_cows@id)]
rm(all_cows); invisible(gc())
M <- pullSnpGeno(gpop, simParam = SP)
rownames(M) <- gpop@id
progress("dosage matrix ready"); cat("Dosage matrix:", nrow(M), "cows x", ncol(M), "SNP; values:",
    paste(sort(unique(as.vector(M))), collapse = ","), "\n")

p   <- colMeans(M) / 2
maf <- pmin(p, 1 - p)
keep <- maf >= 0.01                                    # QC: MAF >= 1%
cat("SNP removed for MAF < 0.01:", sum(!keep), "\n")
M <- M[, keep]; p <- p[keep]
W <- M - 1
Z <- sweep(M, 2, 2 * p)
stopifnot(max(abs(colMeans(Z))) < 1e-10)              # centring check
```

## Genomic relationship matrix G (VanRaden method 1)

$$G = \frac{ZZ'}{2\sum_j p_j(1-p_j)}$$

```{r Gmat}
k2pq <- 2 * sum(p * (1 - p))
G <- tcrossprod(Z) / k2pq
dimnames(G) <- list(rownames(M), rownames(M))
data.table(mean_diag = mean(diag(G)), mean_offdiag = mean(G[upper.tri(G)]),
           sd_diag = sd(diag(G)))
# Cross-check with rrBLUP::A.mat on the -1/0/1 coding (same estimator)
G_rr <- rrBLUP::A.mat(W, min.MAF = 0.01)
cat("max |G - rrBLUP::A.mat| =", signif(max(abs(G - G_rr)), 3), "\n")
```

Centring by the sample's own allele frequencies makes **G singular** (rows of Z sum to zero).
For GBLUP, G is regularised as 0.99 G + 0.01 I (a modelling choice, flagged).

## Pedigree relationship matrix A^-1^ (with inbreeding)

The pedigree is traced `r params$ped_depth` generations back from the analysed cows.
Older ancestors are treated as unrelated base animals.

```{r Ainv}
ped[, `:=`(sire = ifelse(sire %in% id, sire, NA), dam = ifelse(dam %in% id, dam, NA))]
trace_ped <- function(ids, depth) {
  keep <- ids; cur <- ids
  for (d in seq_len(depth)) {
    par <- unique(na.omit(c(ped[id %in% cur, sire], ped[id %in% cur, dam])))
    cur <- setdiff(par, keep); keep <- c(keep, cur)
    if (!length(cur)) break
  }
  keep
}
ped_ids <- trace_ped(dat$id, params$ped_depth)
P <- unique(ped[id %in% ped_ids, .(id, dam, sire)])
P[!(dam %in% id), dam := NA]; P[!(sire %in% id), sire := NA]
P <- as.data.frame(lapply(P, as.character))
Pp <- prepPed(P)                                      # orders parents before offspring
Ai <- makeAinv(Pp)
Ainv <- Ai$Ainv; dimnames(Ainv) <- list(Pp[, 1], Pp[, 1])
F_inb <- setNames(Ai$f, Pp[, 1])
cat("Pedigree animals:", nrow(Pp), "| mean F of analysed cows:",
    round(mean(F_inb[as.character(dat$id)]), 4), "\n")
progress("Ainv built: ", format(Sys.time() - t0))
```

## A~22~, G~22~ compatibility and H^-1^

A~22~^-1^ is obtained without forming A, using the partition of A^-1^
(1 = non-genotyped, 2 = genotyped): A~22~^-1^ = A^22^ - A^21^ (A^11^)^-1^ A^12^.

G is rescaled to the A~22~ base (G\* = a + bG, matching the mean diagonal and mean of A~22~;
Christensen et al. 2012, *Animal*) and blended G~b~ = 0.95 G\* + 0.05 A~22~
(the 0.95/0.05 weighting is a common choice, flagged).

```{r Hinv}
gid <- rownames(G); oid <- setdiff(rownames(Ainv), gid)
A11 <- Ainv[oid, oid]; A12 <- Ainv[oid, gid]; A22u <- Ainv[gid, gid]
# sparse Cholesky of A11 with a DENSE right-hand side (a sparse RHS causes heavy fill-in)
L11 <- Cholesky(forceSymmetric(A11), LDL = FALSE)
A22inv <- as.matrix(A22u) - crossprod(as.matrix(A12), as.matrix(solve(L11, as.matrix(A12))))
progress("A22^-1 built: ", format(Sys.time() - t0))
rm(A11, A12, A22u, L11); invisible(gc())
A22 <- solve(A22inv); dimnames(A22) <- list(gid, gid)

tune_G <- function(Gm) {
  b <- (mean(diag(A22)) - mean(A22)) / (mean(diag(Gm)) - mean(Gm))
  a <- mean(A22) - b * mean(Gm)
  a + b * Gm
}
make_Hinv <- function(Gm) {
  Gb  <- 0.95 * tune_G(Gm) + 0.05 * A22
  # H^-1 = A^-1 + [0, 0; 0, Gb^-1 - A22^-1], built as ONE sparse addition
  # (block assignment Hi[gid, gid] <- ... into a sparse matrix is extremely slow)
  D   <- solve(Gb) - A22inv
  idx <- match(gid, rownames(Ainv)); ng <- length(idx)
  Dsp <- sparseMatrix(i = rep(idx, times = ng), j = rep(idx, each = ng), x = as.vector(D),
                      dims = dim(Ainv), dimnames = dimnames(Ainv))
  forceSymmetric(Ainv + Dsp)
}
Hinv <- make_Hinv(G)
cat("H^-1 dimension:", nrow(Hinv), "| cor(offdiag G, offdiag A22):",
    round(cor(G[upper.tri(G)], A22[upper.tri(A22)]), 3), "\n")
progress("Hinv built: ", format(Sys.time() - t0))
```

**Correction to the record (7 Nov 2026).** An earlier text said that no adjustment of G to A~22~ was
tested. That was wrong: the `tune_G()` step above has always rescaled G as a + bG to the mean
diagonal and mean of A~22~ (Christensen et al. 2012, *Animal* 6:1565; same idea as Vitezica et al.
2011, *Genet Res* 93:357). It does this **once for all three breeds pooled**. What had not been
tested is a model that handles the three breeds as separate base populations. That is what the
metafounder model below adds.

## Metafounder single-step (ssGBLUP_MF)

**Why this second model.** Pedigree relationships assume that all base animals are unrelated and come
from one population. Genomic relationships (VanRaden G) are centred on the allele frequencies of the
genotyped cows, which mix three breeds. The pooled a + bG rescaling fixes the overall mean and
diagonal, but it cannot make the between-breed blocks of G and A~22~ agree at the same time as the
within-breed blocks. Metafounders (Legarra et al. 2015, *Genetics* 200:455; Garcia-Baccino et al.
2017, *Genet Sel Evol* 49:34) solve this by giving each breed its own "base animal" (one metafounder
per breed), with relationships among the metafounders in a matrix **Γ**. Then:

* the pedigree matrix becomes A^Γ, in which base animals of breed i are related to each other by
  γ~ii~ and to base animals of breed j by γ~ij~;
* G is computed with allele frequency 0.5 for every SNP, G~05~ = (M - 1)(M - 1)' / (m/2), so it needs
  no centring and no rescaling: G~05~ and A^Γ~22~ are on the same scale by construction.

**Γ from base allele frequencies** (Legarra et al. 2015, eq. for multiple metafounders):
γ~ij~ = (8/m) Σ~k~ (p~ik~ - 0.5)(p~jk~ - 0.5), with p~ik~ the frequency of SNP k in the base
population of breed i. The base population of a breed is the generation before its base animals in
the truncated pedigree (file 01 saved the cow allele frequencies of every generation). **Flag:** in this
simulation the base frequencies are known exactly; with real data they must be estimated
(e.g. Garcia-Baccino et al. 2017), so the MF result here is a best case for that model.

**A^Γ inverse.** Each animal i with parents s and d (a metafounder replaces an unknown parent of the
same breed) has Mendelian-sampling variance D~i~ = 1 - (a~ss~ + a~dd~)/4, where a metafounder has
a~mm~ = γ~mm~. Then (A^Γ)^-1^ = T' blockdiag(Γ^-1^, D^-1^) T, with T = I - P (P holds 0.5 for each
parent). The diagonal a~ii~ is computed from the rows of the Cholesky-type factor
L, row~i~ = (row~s~ + row~d~)/2 + sqrt(D~i~) e~i~ (Henderson 1976 recursion, with Γ in place of I for
the base).

```{r Hinv_MF}
snpf <- fread(file.path(params$sim_dir, "snp_freq_by_generation.csv"))
pinfo <- ped[match(Pp[, 1], as.character(id)), .(id = as.character(id), breed, generation)]
stopifnot(!anyNA(pinfo$breed))
mf_names <- paste0("MF_", levels(dat$breed))
# base generation(s): one slot per missing parent, frequency of the generation before the animal
miss <- data.table(breed = pinfo$breed, g = pmax(pinfo$generation - 1L, 0L),
                   n = is.na(Pp[, 2]) + is.na(Pp[, 3]))[n > 0, .(n = sum(n)), by = .(breed, g)]
snp_keep <- which(keep)                                 # same MAF subset as G
p_base <- sapply(levels(dat$breed), function(b) {
  w <- miss[breed == b]
  f <- snpf[breed == b & generation %in% w$g & snp %in% snp_keep]
  f <- merge(f, w[, .(generation = g, n)], by = "generation")
  f[, .(p = sum(p * n) / sum(n)), by = snp][order(snp)]$p
})
m_snp <- nrow(p_base)
Gam <- 8 * crossprod(p_base - 0.5) / m_snp
dimnames(Gam) <- list(mf_names, mf_names)
kable(Gam, digits = 3, caption = "Gamma: relationships among the breed metafounders")
kable(miss[order(breed, g)], caption = "Base generation(s) used per breed (n = missing-parent slots)")

# augmented pedigree: metafounders first, then animals (Pp order)
nm  <- length(mf_names); na_ <- nrow(Pp)
all_id <- c(mf_names, Pp[, 1]); pos <- setNames(seq_along(all_id), all_id)
mf_of <- pos[paste0("MF_", pinfo$breed)]
s_i <- ifelse(is.na(Pp[, 3]), mf_of, pos[Pp[, 3]])     # prepPed columns: id, dam, sire
d_i <- ifelse(is.na(Pp[, 2]), mf_of, pos[Pp[, 2]])
stopifnot(all(s_i < nm + seq_len(na_)), all(d_i < nm + seq_len(na_)))   # parents before offspring

# rows of the factor L (A = L L'), stored sparsely as named vectors
Lc <- t(chol(Gam))
rows <- vector("list", nm + na_); aii <- numeric(nm + na_); Dv <- numeric(na_)
for (k in seq_len(nm)) { rows[[k]] <- setNames(Lc[k, seq_len(k)], seq_len(k)); aii[k] <- Gam[k, k] }
for (i in seq_len(na_)) {
  k <- nm + i; s <- s_i[i]; d <- d_i[i]
  Dv[i] <- 1 - (aii[s] + aii[d]) / 4
  v <- c(rows[[s]] / 2, rows[[d]] / 2)
  v <- tapply(v, names(v), sum)
  r <- c(v, setNames(sqrt(Dv[i]), k))
  rows[[k]] <- r; aii[k] <- sum(r^2)
}
stopifnot(all(Dv > 0))
Tm <- sparseMatrix(i = c(seq_len(nm + na_), nm + seq_len(na_), nm + seq_len(na_)),
                   j = c(seq_len(nm + na_), s_i, d_i),
                   x = c(rep(1, nm + na_), rep(-0.5, 2 * na_)), dims = c(nm + na_, nm + na_))
Lam <- bdiag(solve(Gam), Diagonal(x = 1 / Dv))
AinvG <- forceSymmetric(crossprod(Tm, Lam %*% Tm)); dimnames(AinvG) <- list(all_id, all_id)

# check: A^Gamma column from L times A^Gamma inverse must give a unit vector
Lsp <- sparseMatrix(i = rep(seq_along(rows), lengths(rows)),
                    j = as.integer(unlist(lapply(rows, names))), x = unlist(rows),
                    dims = c(nm + na_, nm + na_))
chk_j <- sample(nm + seq_len(na_), 5)
Acol <- Lsp %*% t(Lsp[chk_j, , drop = FALSE])
cat("max |A^G^-1 A^G - I| on 5 test columns:",
    signif(max(abs(as.matrix(AinvG %*% Acol) - diag(1, nm + na_)[, chk_j])), 3), "\n")
F_mf <- setNames(aii[nm + seq_len(na_)] - 1, Pp[, 1])
cat("Mean F of analysed cows: pedigree", round(mean(F_inb[as.character(dat$id)]), 4),
    "| with metafounders", round(mean(F_mf[as.character(dat$id)]), 4), "\n")

# G with allele frequency 0.5 (no centring, no rescaling)
Mk  <- M - 1
G05 <- tcrossprod(Mk) / (ncol(Mk) / 2); dimnames(G05) <- dimnames(G)
stopifnot(ncol(Mk) == m_snp)

# A22^Gamma inverse by partition (block 1 = metafounders + non-genotyped animals)
oidG <- setdiff(all_id, gid)
L11g <- Cholesky(forceSymmetric(AinvG[oidG, oidG]), LDL = FALSE)
A12g <- as.matrix(AinvG[oidG, gid])
A22Ginv <- as.matrix(AinvG[gid, gid]) - crossprod(A12g, as.matrix(solve(L11g, A12g)))
A22G <- solve(A22Ginv); dimnames(A22G) <- list(gid, gid)
rm(L11g, A12g); invisible(gc())

make_Hinv_MF <- function(Gm) {
  D   <- solve(0.95 * Gm + 0.05 * A22G) - A22Ginv
  idx <- match(gid, rownames(AinvG)); ng <- length(idx)
  Dsp <- sparseMatrix(i = rep(idx, times = ng), j = rep(idx, each = ng), x = as.vector(D),
                      dims = dim(AinvG), dimnames = dimnames(AinvG))
  forceSymmetric(AinvG + Dsp)
}
Hinv_MF <- make_Hinv_MF(G05)

# compatibility of G and A22 by breed block: pooled-tuned G vs A22, and G05 vs A22^Gamma
gbr <- as.character(dat[match(gid, as.character(id)), breed])
blk <- function(X, Y) rbindlist(lapply(levels(dat$breed), function(b1) rbindlist(lapply(levels(dat$breed), function(b2) {
  i <- gbr == b1; j <- gbr == b2
  x <- X[i, j]; y <- Y[i, j]
  if (b1 == b2) { x <- x[upper.tri(x)]; y <- y[upper.tri(y)] }
  data.table(block = paste(b1, b2, sep = "-"), mean_G = mean(x), mean_A22 = mean(y))
}))))[!duplicated(sapply(strsplit(block, "-"), function(z) paste(sort(z), collapse = "-")))]
comp <- merge(blk(tune_G(G), A22)[, .(block, pooled_G = mean_G, pooled_A22 = mean_A22)],
              blk(G05, A22G)[, .(block, MF_G05 = mean_G, MF_A22G = mean_A22)], by = "block")
comp[, `:=`(gap_pooled = pooled_G - pooled_A22, gap_MF = MF_G05 - MF_A22G)]
kable(comp, digits = 3, caption = "Mean off-diagonal relationship by breed block: G vs A22 (a smaller gap = more compatible)")
fwrite(comp, file.path(params$sim_dir, "G_A22_compatibility.csv"))
progress("Hinv_MF built: ", format(Sys.time() - t0))
```

# Model functions

All sommer models use the same call; only the relationship inverse changes.

```{r fit_fns}
# breed + herd x generation, or herd x generation alone when every herd-generation holds one breed
# (single-breed herds: breed is then a linear combination of the hg columns)
fixed_formula <- function(d) if (all(d[, uniqueN(breed), by = hg]$V1 == 1)) y ~ hg else y ~ breed + hg

as_gu <- function(Ki) { Ki <- as(Ki, "CsparseMatrix"); attr(Ki, "inverse") <- TRUE; Ki }

fit_sommer <- function(d, Kinv, trait) {
  ids <- rownames(Kinv)
  d <- copy(d)[id %in% ids]
  d[, idf := factor(as.character(id), levels = ids)]
  d[, y := get(trait)]
  fit <- mmes(fixed_formula(d), random = ~vsm(ism(idf), Gu = as_gu(Kinv)),
              rcov = ~units, data = as.data.frame(d),
              control = mmes_control(diagnostics = list(verbose = FALSE)))
  th <- unlist(fit$theta)
  # sommer appends levels without records ("additional Gu levels") to the END of u,
  # so u is NOT in rownames(Kinv) order: always index by sommer's own row names
  u <- as.matrix(fit$u); stopifnot(!is.null(rownames(u)), setequal(rownames(u), ids))
  list(ebv = setNames(u[, 1], rownames(u))[ids], varA = th[1], varE = th[2])
}

Gi_reg <- solve(0.99 * G + 0.01 * diag(nrow(G)))
dimnames(Gi_reg) <- dimnames(G)

# SNP effects back-solved from GBLUP: u_snp = Z' G^-1 a / (2 sum pq)
snp_from_gblup <- function(a_hat, Gm_inv) as.vector(crossprod(Z, Gm_inv %*% a_hat)) / k2pq

# Full-rank fixed-effect design: drop unused levels, then QR-pivot out dependent columns
fullrank_X <- function(d) {
  X <- model.matrix(~ breed + hg, data = droplevels(as.data.frame(d)))
  q <- qr(X); X[, q$pivot[seq_len(q$rank)], drop = FALSE]
}
Xfix <- function(d) { X <- fullrank_X(d); X[, colnames(X) != "(Intercept)", drop = FALSE] }

fit_rrblup <- function(dtr, trait) {
  ms <- mixed.solve(dtr[[trait]], Z = W[as.character(dtr$id), ],
                    X = fullrank_X(dtr))
  list(u = ms$u, varA = ms$Vu * k2pq, varE = ms$Ve)   # var_a = Vu * sum(2pq)
}

fit_bglr <- function(dtr, trait, model) {
  tmp <- tempfile("bglr_"); dir.create(tmp)
  fm <- BGLR(y = dtr[[trait]],
             ETA = list(list(X = Xfix(dtr), model = "FIXED"),
                        list(X = W[as.character(dtr$id), ], model = model)),
             nIter = params$bayes_iter, burnIn = params$bayes_burn,
             saveAt = paste0(tmp, "/"), verbose = FALSE)
  list(u = fm$ETA[[2]]$b, varE = fm$varE)
}
```

# Variance components and heritability recovery (all 10 traits, GBLUP)

Simulated "true" h^2^ for the analysed cows = var(TBV) / var(phenotype within herd-generation),
compared with the GBLUP-REML estimate. This is the parametric check that the models recover
the simulated genetic variance.

```{r vc_all}
h2_mix <- sapply(traits, function(tr) {
  w <- dat[genotyped == TRUE, .N, by = breed]
  sum(w$N * unlist(h2_par[code == tr, as.character(w$breed), with = FALSE])) / sum(w$N)
})
progress("variance components start")
gd <- dat[genotyped == TRUE]
# reference: true h2 WITHIN breed x generation, because breed and herd x generation are
# fitted as fixed effects and absorb between-breed / between-generation genetic differences
true_h2 <- function(dd, tr) {
  t <- dd[[paste0("TBV_", tr)]]; y <- dd[[tr]]
  yc <- y - ave(y, dd$herd, dd$generation)
  var(t - ave(t, dd$breed, dd$generation)) / var(yc - ave(yc, dd$breed, dd$generation))
}
vc <- if (!isTRUE(params$run_vc)) data.table() else rbindlist(lapply(traits, function(tr) {
  fg <- fit_sommer(gd, Gi_reg, tr)                 # genomic REML (genotyped cows)
  fa <- fit_sommer(dat, Ainv, tr)                  # pedigree REML (all phenotyped cows)
  progress("VC ", tr, " done ", format(Sys.time() - t0))
  data.table(trait = tr,
             h2_GBLUP_REML = fg$varA / (fg$varA + fg$varE),
             h2_ABLUP_REML = fa$varA / (fa$varA + fa$varE),
             h2_true_genotyped = true_h2(gd, tr),
             h2_true_all = true_h2(dat, tr),
             h2_assumed_file00 = h2_mix[[tr]])
}))
kable(vc, digits = 3)
```

**Diagnostic for under-estimation.** If h^2^ from GBLUP is below the true value while ABLUP is
close to it, the gap is variance not captured by the SNP panel (genomic heritability is
expected to be lower than h^2^ when markers do not fully tag QTL; de los Campos et al. 2015,
*PLoS Genet* 11:e1005048). If **both** are low, the likely cause is selection in earlier
generations on records not included in this analysis, which biases REML downward (REML is
unbiased under selection only when the data used for selection are in the analysis).

# Cross-validation

Two validation schemes, matching the pipeline timeline (calves genotyped in year 2,
CFIT phenotypes only from year 4):

* **Forward:** train on generations `r head(gens, -1)`; predict the youngest generation
  (`r tail(gens, 1)`) with their phenotypes masked. This mirrors predicting calves before they are recorded.
* **k-fold:** `r params$n_folds` random folds of the genotyped cows, stratified by breed x country x generation.

Metrics, computed on validation cows only:

* `acc_TBV` = cor(EBV, TBV) - true accuracy (available only because this is a simulation);
* `PA` = cor(EBV, y\*) with y\* = phenotype minus its herd-generation mean (what real data allow);
* `acc_PA` = PA / sqrt(h^2^) using the file-00 h^2^ for the breed mix;
* `acc_within_breed` = cor(EBV, TBV) within each breed, averaged with weights n per breed. This is
  the accuracy that matters for ranking candidates, because selection is within breed. The pooled
  `acc_TBV` also rewards or penalises breed-level offsets in the EBVs;
* `slope` = regression of TBV on EBV (1 = unbiased; < 1 = over-dispersed).
* `h2_REML_fit` = h^2^ implied by the variance components that REML estimated in that training set
  (BayesA/B: not applicable). A value near 0 means REML reached the boundary and the EBVs are
  shrunk to almost nothing, which shows up as a near-zero accuracy and slope.

```{r cv_setup}
gd[, fold := NA_integer_]
gd[, fold := sample(rep(seq_len(params$n_folds), length.out = .N)),
   by = .(breed, country, generation)]
schemes <- c(list(forward = gd[generation == max(gens), id]),
             lapply(seq_len(params$n_folds), function(k) gd[fold == k, id]))
names(schemes)[-1] <- paste0("fold", seq_len(params$n_folds))
for (tr in traits) dat[, paste0("ys_", tr) := get(tr) - mean(get(tr)), by = hg]

```

```{r cv_run}
score <- function(ebv, val, tr) {
  v <- dat[id %in% val]
  e <- ebv[as.character(v$id)]
  tbv <- v[[paste0("TBV_", tr)]]; ys <- v[[paste0("ys_", tr)]]
  # within-breed accuracy (selection in file 04 is within breed), weighted by n per breed
  wb <- data.table(b = v$breed, e = e, t = tbv)[, .(r = cor(e, t), n = .N), by = b]
  data.table(acc_TBV = cor(e, tbv), acc_within_breed = sum(wb$r * wb$n) / sum(wb$n),
             PA = cor(e, ys),
             acc_PA = cor(e, ys) / sqrt(h2_mix[[tr]]),
             slope = unname(coef(lm(tbv ~ e))[2]))
}

res <- list(); ebv_fwd <- list()
for (tr in params$focus_traits) for (sc in names(schemes)) {
  val <- schemes[[sc]]
  dtr <- copy(dat)[!(id %in% val)]                  # masked = removed from training data
  gtr <- dtr[genotyped == TRUE]
  out <- list(); h2f <- list(); secs <- list()      # h2f: h2 implied by each REML fit; secs: fit time
  h2_of <- function(f) unname(f$varA / (f$varA + f$varE))
  # ABLUP (pedigree, REML)
  f <- fit_sommer(dtr, Ainv, tr);    out$ABLUP <- f$ebv; h2f$ABLUP <- h2_of(f)
  # GBLUP (REML) and the same prediction via back-solved SNP effects
  f <- fit_sommer(gtr, Gi_reg, tr);  out$GBLUP <- f$ebv; h2f$GBLUP <- h2f$GBLUP_snp <- h2_of(f)
  u_snp <- snp_from_gblup(f$ebv[gid], Gi_reg)
  out$GBLUP_snp <- setNames(as.vector(Z %*% u_snp), gid)
  # ssGBLUP
  tm <- system.time(f <- fit_sommer(dtr, Hinv, tr))[["elapsed"]]
  out$ssGBLUP <- f$ebv; h2f$ssGBLUP <- h2_of(f); secs$ssGBLUP <- tm
  # ssGBLUP with breed metafounders (G05 and A^Gamma; no G rescaling)
  tm <- system.time(f <- fit_sommer(dtr, Hinv_MF, tr))[["elapsed"]]
  out$ssGBLUP_MF <- f$ebv; h2f$ssGBLUP_MF <- h2_of(f); secs$ssGBLUP_MF <- tm
  # weighted ssGBLUP (Wang et al. 2012): 2 iterations; each re-fits ssGBLUP with the new
  # SNP weights. Weights use EBVs of genotyped TRAINING cows only (no validation leakage).
  train_g <- intersect(gid, as.character(gtr$id))
  d_snp <- rep(1, ncol(Z)); a_tr <- f$ebv[train_g]
  for (it in 1:2) {
    Gd_tr <- tcrossprod(sweep(Z[train_g, ], 2, sqrt(d_snp), `*`)) / k2pq
    u0 <- d_snp * as.vector(crossprod(Z[train_g, ],
                  solve(Gd_tr + 0.01 * diag(length(train_g)), a_tr))) / k2pq
    d_snp <- u0^2 * 2 * p * (1 - p); d_snp <- d_snp / mean(d_snp)
    Gw <- tcrossprod(sweep(Z, 2, sqrt(d_snp), `*`)) / k2pq; dimnames(Gw) <- dimnames(G)
    fw <- fit_sommer(dtr, make_Hinv(Gw), tr); a_tr <- fw$ebv[train_g]
  }
  out$wssGBLUP <- fw$ebv; h2f$wssGBLUP <- h2_of(fw)
  # rrBLUP (SNP effects)
  f <- fit_rrblup(gtr, tr)
  out$rrBLUP <- setNames(as.vector(W %*% f$u), gid); h2f$rrBLUP <- h2_of(f)
  # BayesA / BayesB (SNP effects)
  for (m in c("BayesA", "BayesB")) {
    f <- fit_bglr(gtr, tr, m)
    out[[m]] <- setNames(as.vector(W %*% f$u), gid)
  }
  if (sc == "forward") {                            # keep forward EBVs for inspection
    v <- dat[id %in% val, c("id", "breed", paste0("TBV_", tr)), with = FALSE]
    setnames(v, 3, "TBV")
    for (m in names(out)) v[, (m) := out[[m]][as.character(id)]]
    ebv_fwd[[tr]] <- cbind(trait = tr, v)
  }
  for (m in names(out)) res[[paste(tr, sc, m)]] <-
    cbind(data.table(trait = tr, scheme = sc, model = m), score(out[[m]], val, tr),
          h2_REML_fit = if (is.null(h2f[[m]])) NA_real_ else h2f[[m]],
          fit_sec = if (is.null(secs[[m]])) NA_real_ else secs[[m]])
  progress(tr, " ", sc, " done ", format(Sys.time() - t0))
}
res <- rbindlist(res)
```

**Sanity check:** `GBLUP` and `GBLUP_snp` must give identical accuracies, because predicting
from back-solved SNP effects is algebraically equivalent to GBLUP.

```{r check_equiv}
chk <- dcast(res[model %in% c("GBLUP", "GBLUP_snp")], trait + scheme ~ model, value.var = "acc_TBV")
chk[, diff := abs(GBLUP - GBLUP_snp)]
kable(chk, digits = 4)
```

# Results

```{r results_table}
summ <- res[model != "GBLUP_snp",
            .(acc_TBV = mean(acc_TBV), acc_TBV_sd = sd(acc_TBV),
              acc_within_breed = mean(acc_within_breed),
              PA = mean(PA), acc_PA = mean(acc_PA), slope = mean(slope),
              h2_fit_min = min(h2_REML_fit), h2_fit_max = max(h2_REML_fit)),
            by = .(trait, model, scheme_type = ifelse(scheme == "forward", "forward", "k-fold"))]
kable(summ[order(trait, scheme_type, -acc_TBV)], digits = 3,
      caption = "Mean accuracy by trait, model and validation scheme (sd across folds)")
```

```{r results_plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
ggplot(res[model != "GBLUP_snp" & scheme != "forward"],
       aes(model, acc_TBV, fill = model)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = res[model != "GBLUP_snp" & scheme == "forward"],
             shape = 4, size = 3, colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~trait) +
  labs(y = "cor(EBV, TBV)", x = NULL,
       title = "Accuracy across k-fold CV (boxes) and forward validation (x)") +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

## Which single-step model is more reliable?

Both single-step models use the same data, pedigree and REML. They differ only in how the genomic and
pedigree relationships are made compatible: pooled a + bG rescaling (`ssGBLUP`) versus breed
metafounders (`ssGBLUP_MF`). **Decision rule (mine, fixed before seeing the result):**

1. Primary criterion: mean **within-breed accuracy** over all focus traits and validation sets, because
   selection in file 04 is within breed.
2. If the two differ by less than one standard error of the paired difference, the accuracies are
   treated as equal and the model whose **dispersion slope** is closer to 1 wins (less bias in
   EBV scale, which matters when EBVs of different breeds or ages are compared).

The chosen model is written to `ssgblup_choice_<focus traits>.csv` and is the single-step model used in file 04.

```{r ss_choice}
pw <- dcast(res[model %in% c("ssGBLUP", "ssGBLUP_MF")], trait + scheme ~ model,
            value.var = c("acc_within_breed", "slope", "fit_sec"))
pw[, d_acc := acc_within_breed_ssGBLUP_MF - acc_within_breed_ssGBLUP]
se_d <- sd(pw$d_acc) / sqrt(nrow(pw))
ss_sum <- data.table(model = c("ssGBLUP", "ssGBLUP_MF"),
  acc_within_breed = c(mean(pw$acc_within_breed_ssGBLUP), mean(pw$acc_within_breed_ssGBLUP_MF)),
  mean_abs_slope_dev = c(mean(abs(pw$slope_ssGBLUP - 1)), mean(abs(pw$slope_ssGBLUP_MF - 1))),
  mean_fit_sec = c(mean(pw$fit_sec_ssGBLUP), mean(pw$fit_sec_ssGBLUP_MF)))
kable(ss_sum, digits = 3, caption = "Single-step variants, averaged over traits and validation sets")
md <- mean(pw$d_acc)
winner <- if (abs(md) >= se_d) { if (md > 0) "ssGBLUP_MF" else "ssGBLUP" } else
  ss_sum[which.min(mean_abs_slope_dev), model]
reason <- if (abs(md) >= se_d) "within-breed accuracy differs by at least 1 SE" else
  "accuracies equal within 1 SE; slope closer to 1"
fwrite(data.table(winner = winner, reason = reason, mean_diff_acc_MF_minus_pooled = md, se_diff = se_d,
                  focus_traits = paste(params$focus_traits, collapse = ",")),
       file.path(params$sim_dir, paste0("ssgblup_choice_", paste(params$focus_traits, collapse = "_"), ".csv")))
```

**Result:** mean within-breed accuracy difference (MF minus pooled) = `r round(md, 3)`
(SE `r round(se_d, 3)`); chosen model: **`r winner`** (`r reason`).

## Theoretical expectation (sanity check, not a result)

Expected accuracy from Daetwyler et al. (2008, *PLoS ONE* 3:e3395),
r = sqrt(N h^2^ / (N h^2^ + M~e~)), with M~e~ = 2 N~e~ L / log(4 N~e~ L) (Goddard 2009, *Genetica*).
N~e~ = 90 (CATTLE history), L = genome length in Morgans of the simulated chromosomes (29 since 7 Nov 2026).
This formula assumes one homogeneous population, so it is only a rough reference here.

```{r theory}
L  <- sum(sapply(SP$genMap, function(x) max(x)))
Ne <- 90
Me <- 2 * Ne * L / log(4 * Ne * L)
N_train <- nrow(gd) * (params$n_folds - 1) / params$n_folds
theo <- data.table(trait = params$focus_traits,
                   h2 = h2_mix[params$focus_traits])
theo[, r_expected := sqrt(N_train * h2 / (N_train * h2 + Me))]
cat("Genome length L =", round(L, 2), "M | Me =", round(Me), "| N_train =", N_train, "\n")
kable(theo, digits = 3)
```
